Air Charter Safety Foundation (ACSF) expands Aviation Safety Action Program (ASAP) with addition of Novus Jet Charter and Otter Air Services — April 18, 2024

By Luciano Braganca 16Dec2024

About Novus Jet Charter

Type: Business/Private Charter
Base: Stuart Witham
Aircraft: 2

Novus Jet Charter (Stuart Witham) expanded its Part 135-certified fleet in November 2024 with the addition of a first Challenger 300. The aircraft is expected to commence charter services at the beginning of January 2025, president Eric Sanchez confirmed to ch-aviation.

N776CJ (msn 20107) is an 18.6-year-old aircraft, which joins a 22.7-year-old Learjet 60 under Novus Jet Charter's Part 135 certificate. The Learjet 60, inducted in June, replaced at the time a 30-year-old Learjet 31A.

"We are seeking additional aircraft to bring under management and plan to slowly expand our fleet," Sanchez told ch-aviation, without elaborating on the types.

Originally delivered to Canada's Skyservice Business Aviation, the Bombardier Business Aircraft midsize jet was most recently operated by Jet Linx Aviation. It last flew for the operator under the 'JTL' code on July 25 from Lakeland to Boca Raton.

Novus Jet Charter Expands Fleet with First Challenger 300
=========================================================

Novus Jet Charter has expanded its Part 135-certified fleet with the addition of its first Challenger 300, which is set to begin charter services in January 2025, according to president Eric Sanchez. The newly acquired aircraft, N776CJ (msn 20107), is 18.6 years old and adds to the company's existing fleet, which includes a 22.7-year-old Learjet 60.

The Learjet 60, which was inducted in June 2024, replaced a 30-year-old Learjet 31A, marking a significant update for Novus Jet Charter's fleet. The company plans to continue its gradual expansion by seeking additional aircraft to bring under management, although Sanchez declined to specify which types of aircraft will be added in the future.
